# Color

Every color is a --ds token named for its job.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Colors.mdx`

## Overview

Every color is a semantic token named for the job it does: page text, field edge, or primary button fill. Each token resolves per mode, so components adapt to light, dark and increased contrast automatically.

```css
color: var(--ds-text-danger);
background: var(--ds-background-danger-subtler);
```

Figma holds them in `color / semantics` (modes Light, Dark, Light IC and Dark IC); `color / primitives` stay hidden. See Tokens: Color for the full collection.

## How the tokens are built

Primitives hold raw ramps and stay hidden; bind only semantic tokens. Names read from general to specific: property, role, emphasis, state. In Figma, parts join with slashes (`color/background/danger/bold/hovered`); in CSS, drop `color` and join with dashes behind `--ds-` (`--ds-background-danger-bold-hovered`).

| Part | In `color/background/danger/bold/hovered` | Values | What it says |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| color | Namespace | `color` | Dropped in CSS. Surface and shadow tokens start with elevation. |
| background | Property | `text` · `icon` · `border` · `background` · `link` · `surface` · `shadow` · `blanket` · `skeleton` · `interaction` · `chart` | What the color paints. |
| danger | Role | `brand` · `neutral` · `selected` · `input` · `inverse` · `disabled` · `focused` · `danger` · `warning` · `success` · `information` · `discovery` · `accent-*` · `competency-*` | What it means. Omitted for default neutral. |
| bold | Emphasis | `subtlest` · `subtler` · `subtle` · (default) · `bold` · `bolder` · `boldest` | Contrast against the surface. |
| hovered | State | `hovered` · `pressed` · `visited` | Interactive backgrounds and links only. |

`--ds-border-<role>-subtle` is the pale edge of an outlined label, such as a Tag or a date Status.

## Modes

PLUS ships four modes: light and dark, each at standard and increased contrast. `auto` follows OS `prefers-color-scheme` and `prefers-contrast`.

- **Dark mode** is not light inverted: raised and overlay surfaces step lighter as they rise, because shadows are subtle on dark grounds. Design in dark mode by choosing the same token; never map your own values.
- **Increased contrast** pushes text to 7:1 and borders, icons and the focus ring to 4.5:1. Tints, surfaces and the Blanket stay unchanged.
- **In code**, set `data-color-mode` (`light`, `dark`, `auto`) and `data-contrast-mode` (`no-preference`, `more`, `auto`) on `<html>`. No attribute means light at standard contrast.
- **In Figma**, set the frame mode to Light, Dark, Light IC or Dark IC.

## Roles

Pick the role for the intention, then the emphasis. Never pick a role by how the hue looks or by a matching value: a danger fill, its border and its icon are three tokens even when two of them share a value today.

| Role | Default fill | Text | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `neutral` | `--ds-background-neutral` | `--ds-text-subtle` | Default text, secondary buttons and navigation. |
| `brand` | `--ds-background-brand-bold` | `--ds-text-brand` | Primary actions and brand marks. |
| `information` | `--ds-background-information-bold` | `--ds-text-information` | Informative UI or work in progress. |
| `success` | `--ds-background-success-bold` | `--ds-text-success` | A completed or favorable outcome, such as a booked session. |
| `warning` | `--ds-background-warning-bold` | `--ds-text-warning` | Caution before a mistake happens. Bold warning uses --ds-text-warning-inverse. |
| `danger` | `--ds-background-danger-bold` | `--ds-text-danger` | Errors or destructive actions, such as a failed payment. |
| `discovery` | `--ds-background-discovery-bold` | `--ds-text-discovery` | New features, onboarding or a Suggestion. |
| `accent` | `--ds-background-accent-teal-subtle` | `--ds-text-accent-teal` | Categorization without status meaning. |
| `inverse` | — | `--ds-text-inverse` | Text, icons and borders on bold backgrounds. |
| `input` | `--ds-background-input` | `--ds-text` | Form fields. |

Danger, warning, success, information and discovery each ship four emphasis levels: default tint for a Banner, `subtler` for a Status tag, `subtle` for a non-interactive Tag, and `bold` for a filled Count tag or button.

## Accent hues

Eleven hues decorate tags, charts, avatars and illustrations. An accent hue carries no status meaning; when color carries meaning, use a role.

## Competency areas

The five competency areas each have their own role (`social-emotional` orange, `mastering-content` teal, `advocacy` lime, `relationship` magenta, `technology-tools` brown): `background/competency/<subject>` with `text/competency/<subject>` and `border/competency/<subject>` for a Tag, `subtle` for illustration bodies, and `bold` for filled marks. Use a competency color only for its area.

## Surfaces and border

| Token | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `--ds-surface` | The page |
| `--ds-surface-sunken` | Grouped grounds: sidebar column, sunken well |
| `--ds-surface-raised` | Cards, paired with `--ds-shadow-raised` |
| `--ds-surface-overlay` | Modals, menus, popups, tooltips and flags, paired with `--ds-shadow-overlay` |
| `--ds-border` | Standard dividers; `--ds-border-bold` bounds controls |

A surface lifts by shadow, never by a different gray. Surface levels and shadows are owned by Elevation; stroke widths and the focus ring are owned by Border.

## States

Hover and press step along the token's own ladder. Focus is always a ring, never a fill (Border). AI color tokens live on AI UI › Color.

- **Rows, menu items and sidebar items** take `color/background/neutral/subtle/hovered` and `/pressed`.
- **Selected elements** take `color/background/selected` (`selected/hovered` and `/pressed` on interaction), paired with a second cue such as a check mark or border. Never use brand, link or focused tokens for selection. Keep selected and focused distinct: selected persists to show a current choice, focus shows where the keyboard is, and a selected item stays recognizable while hovered or pressed.
- **Fields** take `color/background/input/hovered` with `color/border/input` on hover; on focus they keep their fill and add the focus ring.
- **Icons** have no hovered or pressed color tokens; show interaction with a subtle neutral background behind the icon.
- **Avatars and images** whose fill cannot change use `color/interaction/hovered` and `color/interaction/pressed` overlays.

```css
.my-element:hover {
  background-color: var(--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered);
}
.my-element:active {
  background-color: var(--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed);
}
.my-element.is-selected {
  background-color: var(--ds-background-selected);
}
```

## Partner pairs and contrast

Every foreground token pairs with a ground that clears WCAG AA across all four modes: 4.5:1 for text (7:1 in IC) and 3:1 for icons, borders and the focus ring (4.5:1 in IC).

- **Bold fills** take `color/text/inverse` and `color/icon/inverse`, except bold warning which takes dark `color/text/warning/inverse`.
- **Status tints** take the role's text token, or its `-bolder` step on `-subtler` and `-subtle` grounds.
- **Surfaces** take `color/text/default`, `subtle` or `subtlest`.
- Never carry meaning by color alone: a status has an icon or a word, and a chart has a legend or direct labels. Use 3:1 for UI essential to understanding.

## Data-viz color

Charts use `--chart-*` tokens (`chartPalette` from `@/components`). Never reach for an accent hue or a UI role token to draw a series. Color is the one foundation with chart rules of its own; charts take spacing, radius, elevation, stroke, type, layers and motion from the same component tokens as the rest of the system.

| Job | What it encodes | Tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One series | Single measure | `--chart-brand`; reference line takes `--chart-neutral` |
| Categorical | Distinct series | `--chart-categorical-1` to `-8`, in order |
| Sequential | Magnitude | One hue from `subtler` to `bold`, `bolder`, `boldest` (darkest = largest) |
| Diverging | Direction from a baseline | Two hues around `--ds-background-accent-gray-subtler` (orange and blue by default; never red and green) |
| Status | On track, at risk, off track | `--chart-success`, `-warning`, `-danger`, `-information`, `-discovery` (plus `-bold` for the more extreme level) |
| SMART subject | SMART area | `--chart-smart-&lt;subject&gt;` |

- Use five or six categories at most and group the rest into "Other".
- Never mix categorical and status colors in one chart, and give every series or state a second cue (label, shape, pattern, icon or backing table).
- Titles, axes, gridlines, tooltips and threshold lines wear text and border tokens, never a chart color.

### Categorical order

Assign series in slot order without skipping.

| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark | Light IC | Dark IC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (brand) | lagoon | 600 | 500 | 850 | 300 |
| 2 | orange | 800 | 700 | 1000 | 500 |
| 3 | blue | 500 | 500 | 800 | 300 |
| 4 | magenta | 800 | 700 | 1000 | 500 |
| 5 | lime | 500 | 400 | 800 | 250 |
| 6 | purple | 700 | 700 | 900 | 500 |
| 7 | orange | 500 | 500 | 800 | 300 |
| 8 | blue | 800 | 700 | 1000 | 500 |

Three rules govern this sequence:

- **Brand leads:** slot 1 is lagoon (`--chart-brand`), so a one-series chart and the first series of a multi-series chart share their lead color.
- **Neighbors alternate light and dark steps:** slot 2 (orange-800) sits between slot 1 (lagoon-600) and slot 3 (blue-500), alternating through slot 6 so adjacent series remain distinct in grayscale and under color-vision deficiency.
- **Hues spread across the wheel:** lagoon, orange, blue, magenta, lime and purple never place two adjacent slots in the same hue family. Yellow (warning), red (danger) and teal (too close to brand) stay out; lime and purple-500 double as success and discovery, which is why categorical and status colors never mix.
- **Overflow and dark mode:** slots 7 and 8 reprise orange and blue for overflow past six series. Dark mode steps one lighter except blue (3) and orange (7), which hold at 500 to preserve lightness alternation, and purple (6), which holds at 700 so it does not crowd its neighbors.

### Separators, ramps, SMART subjects and hover

- **Separators:** keep a gap or `--ds-border-inverse` line where marks touch (stacked bars, histogram bins, waterfall steps). Lightness alternation identifies the series; the separator marks the boundary.
- **Sequential and diverging ramps:** sequential runs `--ds-background-accent-<hue>-subtler` through `--chart-<hue>-bold`, `-bolder` and `-boldest` (strongest tone = largest value). Diverging runs two hues around `--ds-background-accent-gray-subtler` (orange and blue by default; never red and green).
- **SMART subjects:** each subject uses the emphasis that keeps S-M-A-R-T neighbors apart: social-emotional orange (`bold`), mastering content teal (`boldest`), advocacy lime (`bold`), relationship magenta (`boldest`), technology tools brown (`bold`). Label directly or keep the legend beside the chart.
- **Labels and hover:** place labels beside marks; when a label must sit on a fill (heatmap cell, stacked segment), use `--ds-text` or `--ds-text-inverse`. Hovered marks take their `-hovered` token, and unselected series fade with `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

## Chart order, targets and ranges

Sort categories from most to least (an ordinal set such as grades takes one hue ramp), put the strongest tone on the largest value, and mark targets and ranges without shading bands or repeating tooltip numbers beside the bar.

### Sort biggest first and darken with the value

Students by grade in the tutoring cohort.

Do: Biggest at the top, darkest tone on the biggest value.
Don't: Grades in any order, one tone; the eye has to read every number to find the biggest.

### Mark the target with a tick and the range with an outline

Attendance for one class against a 90% target.

Do: A green tick at 90 and a green outline on the track.
Don't: A shaded band and a value beside the bar; the band hides the bar's own end and the text repeats the tooltip.

## Disabled

Disabled is a dedicated color token (`color/text/disabled`, `color/background/disabled`, `color/border/disabled`), not an opacity fade. `--ds-opacity-disabled` is reserved for dimmed images and de-emphasized chart series. State the reason a control is disabled in nearby text (see Accessibility).

### Disable with color tokens

The Reschedule button after the session has ended.

Do: Disabled takes color/text/disabled on color/background/disabled.
Don't: Opacity on the primary button; it still looks clickable and the gray is not the system one.

## Links

Links take `color/link/default` (`--ds-link`, with `--ds-link-pressed` on press and no hovered color step). Underline links in running text at rest and on hover; standalone navigation links, menus, buttons and card titles may omit the underline. Never use brand, selected or focused colors for a link.

### Underline links in running text

Do: Link color and underline together.
Don't: The color alone is too close to the body text, so the link is easy to miss.

## Pattern colors

| Pattern | Part | Tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tile | Rest · hovered · selected | `color/background/neutral/subtle` · `…/subtle/hovered` · `color/background/selected` with `color/border/selected` |
| Input | Field · edge · placeholder · helper | `color/background/input` · `color/border/input` · `color/text/subtlest` · `color/text/subtle` |
| Progress and meter | Track · fill | `color/background/neutral` · `color/background/brand/bold` (success or warning bold for status) |
| Empty state | Icon · message | `color/icon/subtlest` · `color/text/subtle` |
| Skeleton | Blocks | `color/skeleton/default` · `color/skeleton/subtle` |
| Table | Grid lines · head rule · selected row | `color/border/default` · `color/border/bold` · `color/background/selected` across the whole row |
| Sidebar item | Hovered · selected | `color/background/neutral/subtle/hovered` · `color/background/selected` with `color/text/selected` and `color/icon/selected` |

## Do and don't

### Use the right role

Pick the role for the job. A failed payment is danger; an accent has no meaning, so it should not carry one.

Do: Danger for a failed payment.
Don't: A purple accent where the color has semantic meaning.

### Pair text with its ground

Take the text color from the same role as the ground. Gray text on a bold ground falls well below 4.5:1 in both modes.

Do: Danger text on the subtle danger ground.
Don't: Gray text on the bold danger ground; the role is right and the pair is wrong.

### Use inverse tokens on bold backgrounds

On a bold fill, text and icons take `color/text/inverse` and `color/icon/inverse` (`color/text/warning/inverse` on bold warning).

Do: color/text/inverse on a bold danger fill.
Don't: color/text/default on a bold fill loses contrast.

### Show focus with a ring, never a fill

A filled field looks selected or disabled. The focus ring is the one signal for keyboard focus.

Do: The field keeps its fill and gains the focus ring, color/border/focused.
Don't: A brand fill on the field to show focus; it reads as a selected value and hides what is typed.

### Keep selected and focused distinct

Selection uses the selected tokens and another cue such as a check mark. The focus ring is only for keyboard focus.

Do: Selected tokens plus a check mark.
Don't: The focus ring used to mean selected.

### One series, one color

A single series is drawn in the brand chart color. Reaching for the categorical set makes a legend that says nothing.

Do: Five weeks of one measure, all in color/chart/brand.
Don't: A rainbow on one measure suggests five series; the color does no job, and a reader looks for a legend that is not there.

## Accessibility

- Foreground/background partner pairs clear WCAG 2.1 AA in all four modes: 4.5:1 for text smaller than 24 px (1.4.3) and 3:1 for essential UI, icons, borders, the focus ring and text 24 px or larger (1.4.11), rising to 7:1 and 4.5:1 in increased contrast.
- Never convey meaning by color alone: pair status colors with an icon or text, selection with a check mark or 2 px border, and chart series with labels, shapes or a table.
- Warning icons and borders use `color/icon/warning` and `color/border/warning` rather than the yellow fill (2.87:1 on the darkest surface) so they clear 3:1.
- Check new screens in all four modes with the toolbar's Color mode and Contrast switches, and see Accessibility for cross-cutting rules.
